audit.sub: Where the account is leaking and where the upside is. All figures Klaviyo-attributed unless noted; windows are the last 12 complete months through Jul 2026. This audit covers campaigns and the automation layer, since the two compound together.

wins.title: Send more campaigns (biggest single opportunity)
wins.detail: Campaigns go out about 3.6 times a month, unevenly. At roughly $6,600 a send and a 47% open rate, a fuller, more consistent rhythm is the biggest single opportunity in the account, well into six figures a year. How far to push is the client's call; the calendar suggests four to six sends a month to start, built from what has worked here.

wins.title: Fix the click rate (47% open, 1.2% click)
wins.detail: 47% of people open, but only 1.2% click. Sharper offers, clearer calls to action, and testing turn that attention into clicks, the biggest revenue lever after send volume.

wins.title: Build the missing retention flows (win-back, review)
wins.detail: Onboarding already covers new-customer post-purchase and Abandoned Cart earns $29 per email. What is missing is win-back for lapsed customers, review requests, back-in-stock, and a replenishment or repeat-purchase nudge, all proven, reliable revenue.

wins.title: Welcome every new subscriber (only 817 sent)
wins.detail: The welcome series converts at $28 per email but delivered only 817 emails against about 1,181 new subscribers a year, because signups are not feeding its entry list. Fixing the entry welcomes every new subscriber through a proven series.

wins.title: Turn on SMS
wins.detail: No SMS runs at all. Abandoned-cart and win-back SMS add strong incremental revenue on top of email.

wins.title: Segment sends instead of full-list blasts
wins.detail: Almost every campaign blasts the full list. Sending to engaged segments protects deliverability and lets us send more often without fatigue.

wins.title: Start A/B testing
wins.detail: No experiments have ever run. Testing compounds every other win, so each send beats the last instead of being a one-off.

audit.title: Account audit

findings.body: The store did about $5.26M over the last 12 months and is still growing, from roughly $367k a month to $481k. Email and SMS drove only 14.4% of that. A well-run lifecycle and campaign program typically drives 25% to 35% of store revenue, often more. Lifting email from 14% to around 28% of store revenue, still only the middle of a healthy range, is worth roughly $700,000 in additional email revenue a year. The wins below are exactly how we close it.
findings.title: Email drives just 14% of a $5.3M store

findings.body: Campaigns go out only about 3.6 times a month, and unevenly, with several months down at one or two. Each send is worth roughly $6,600 at a strong 47% open rate, so lifting cadence is the single biggest opportunity in the account: a fuller, more consistent rhythm could add well into six figures a year, even after discounting for list fatigue. How far to push is your call. The calendar below suggests four to six sends a month for the next three months, built from the angles that have worked here, to make each one count.

items.title: Product spotlight / build feature (like the Power Stroke send)
How-to / install guide that links to the parts (lifts clicks)
Buy Now, Pay Later / financing push
Customer build showcase / UGC ('show us your rig')
Halloween Buy-Now-Pay-Later sale (your Halloween BNPL worked)
Fall bundle / kit offer to lift AOV
Early Black Friday VIP early-access teaser

findings.title: Campaigns: the single biggest opportunity is sending more

findings.body: Campaigns get a strong 47% open rate, but only 1.2% of delivered emails get a click. The attention is there and the emails are landing; the content, offers and calls to action are not turning that attention into clicks. Click rate is the biggest lever on campaign revenue after send volume. Lifting it from 1.2% to a still modest 2.5% roughly doubles the revenue each send produces, well into six figures a year on today's campaign volume.

chart.leak: 47% open, but only 1.2% click. The opens are there, the clicks are not, and that gap is the opportunity.

findings.title: Big opens, almost no clicks

findings.body: Abandoned Cart is a star, about $255k in a year at $29 per email delivered, and the Onboarding flow, which triggers on a first order, already handles new-customer post-purchase at $142k. So automations clearly convert here. But the rest of the retention layer is missing: no win-back for lapsed customers, no review request, no back-in-stock, and no replenishment or repeat-purchase nudge. For a high-consideration, high-AOV catalogue, win-back and a repeat-purchase flow in particular are large, reliable revenue that is not built yet.
findings.title: Key retention flows are missing (win-back, review, back-in-stock)

findings.body: The Welcome flow, which fires when someone joins the list, is the best-converting automation in the account: 65% open, 13% click, about $28 in revenue per email delivered. But it delivered only 817 emails in a whole year. With roughly 1,181 new subscribers a year and a three-email series, it should be delivering closer to 3,500. Most new subscribers are never welcomed, most likely because signups are not feeding the flow's entry list. (The separate Onboarding flow is a post-purchase flow, triggered by a first order, not a subscriber welcome.) Fixing the entry so every new subscriber gets this proven series is low-risk revenue.

findings.title: New subscribers are barely being welcomed

findings.body: Sends go to a near-identical audience every time: the median campaign reaches 13,830 recipients and the largest 15,498, so almost every send is a full-list blast. Sending to engaged segments, and suppressing the unengaged, protects deliverability so the strong opens keep landing, and lets us send more often without fatiguing the list, which is what unlocks the higher cadence in win 1.
findings.title: Every campaign goes to the whole list

findings.body: No SMS is sent, in flows or campaigns. For abandoned-cart and win-back especially, SMS adds strong incremental revenue on top of email. It is a whole channel sitting idle.
findings.title: Zero SMS, an entire channel untapped

findings.body: We checked the account through Klaviyo's API: there are no A/B experiments in any flow, none running now and none ever set up, so every campaign and flow is a guess that never compounds. The reason our longest-serving accounts keep growing is nonstop testing: six tests a week, three subject-line and preview tests and three full design overhauls, at about a 67% win rate that a central brain, aggregating learnings across every account, keeps pushing higher. Losing tests are cut fast and every winner becomes the new baseline, so each send beats the last instead of being a one-off.
findings.title: No A/B testing — we checked, and nothing is learning

findings.body: New subscribers run only about 100 a month, low for a store this size. Campaign reach is a direct function of list size, so slow growth quietly caps campaign revenue no matter how well we send. Stronger capture compounds with the higher cadence in win 1.
findings.title: List growth is slow, and it caps every campaign

findings.body: Everything in this audit is day-to-day work for us: campaign strategy and cadence, the automated flow architecture, list growth, channel expansion, and relentless testing. The wins at the top are the roadmap. Most of our clients sit between $3M and $20M in revenue, with the average around $5M to $8M, but we also work with smaller budgets. We build a package to fit: a baseline of what we typically do, scaled to where you are.
